package_metadata.design_authority: Human (Phase 26/27/28 design + Phase 29 registration review + Phase 30 implementation authorization)

identity.name: TableCellSegmentation
identity.description: L1 STRUCTURAL table capability. Given a Human-confirmed table region and a merged text block (a single table column collapsed into one text block by layout-first PDF slicing), segment the block into individual CELL observations via geometry-only, deterministic row separation. It recovers the per-cell granularity lost during block-level slicing. It performs ZERO semantic association: no header interpretation, no column-meaning inference, no row matching, no cell joining, no fact generation. The L2 semantic layer (which value belongs to which component) remains permanently owned by Human.

scope.problem_space: Type A table fragmentation: multiple table cells merged into a single text block during PDF block-level text extraction, losing per-cell boundaries.
scope.note_f3: table region identification remains Human-assisted (Phase 27 F-3); this capability performs cell segmentation ONLY within a Human-confirmed region.

table_region_reference.description: Human-confirmed table region identity (fact; NOT auto-detected)

bbox.description: block bounding box [x0, y0, x1, y1]

column_index.description: Human-confirmed column index of this block (default 0)

strategy.execution_strategy: GEOMETRY-ONLY ROW SEPARATION: split the merged block text by line boundaries (each line = one row = one cell); assign each cell a proportional geometric bbox slice derived from the block bbox. Describes WHAT structural granularity to recover, NOT how to interpret table meaning.

positive_boundary.definition: Deterministic cell segmentation within a Human-confirmed table region: row boundary detection (line split) and merged-cell geometric split (proportional bbox slice). Output is a list of structural cell observations.
positive_boundary.core_structure: merged block (text + bbox) → per-row cell observations (six structural fields)
positive_boundary.domain_scope: L1 structural table geometry (any domain; no semantic vocabulary)

exclusions.reason: Matching a quantity cell to its component name is semantic interpretation, permanently owned by Human.
Determining what a column MEANS (e.g. 'Volume', 'Quantity') is semantic, not structural.
Joining two cells or matching rows across columns is semantic reconstruction, forbidden.
Producing value/unit/normalized facts is extraction-layer work, not structural segmentation.

activation_rule.trigger: Human supplies a confirmed table_region_reference and a merged block
activation_rule.note: Activation is a Human-driven observation, NOT a Runtime decision; no automatic table detection.

conflicts.resolution: Orthogonal by LAYER: those three are L2 semantic table capabilities (reconstructed_entries / entries / column_types + confidence); CAP-TABLE-CELL-SEGMENT is L1 structural (cell geometry only, zero semantic authority). No mutual exclusion.

validation_criteria.pass_condition: RA101 15-value block recovers 15 cells; output carries exactly six structural fields; zero semantic fields
review_questions: Does the segmentation recover the correct cell count without semantic interpretation?
Does each cell observation carry ONLY the six structural fields (no value/unit/fact)?

evidence.evidence_note: Evidence is EMPTY at IMPLEMENTED status. Phase 30 establishes the deterministic segmenter and its RA101 validation case; promotion metrics are populated by later verification, NOT hand-hardcoded.
